summary: Modern databases and data platforms increasingly embed AI/ML directly into the data layer, enabling in-database model training, LLM inference via SQL functions, and semantic retrieval through vector search — eliminating the need to move data to separate ML systems. Vector search has become a baseline feature for GenAI and RAG workloads, with the vector database market projected to grow at roughly 24% CAGR toward ~$17.9 billion by 2034 as enterprise adoption of vector-based retrieval accelerates. Platforms differentiate by whether vector search is natively built-in versus provided through third-party extensions, and by how tightly they integrate hosted LLMs and embedding models.

databases.name: Snowflake (Cortex AI)
databases.ai_feature: Snowflake Cortex AI — managed LLM and ML functions
databases.description: Cortex provides serverless SQL and Python functions to run LLM tasks (COMPLETE, SUMMARIZE, TRANSLATE, SENTIMENT, EXTRACT_ANSWER), embedding generation, Cortex Search for retrieval, Cortex Analyst for natural-language-to-SQL, and Document AI — all running inside Snowflake's governed environment without moving data. Cortex capabilities are also being extended to Snowflake Postgres.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Snowflake supports a VECTOR data type with VECTOR_COSINE_SIMILARITY / VECTOR_L2_DISTANCE functions and Cortex Search for managed hybrid semantic retrieval, built directly into the platform.
databases.llm_integration: Hosted first-party and partner LLMs (e.g., Anthropic Claude, Meta Llama, Mistral, Snowflake Arctic) callable via Cortex SQL/REST functions; no external API wiring required.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based pricing in Snowflake credits, billed per token for LLM functions and per-query/serving for Cortex Search and embeddings; no separate license beyond standard Snowflake compute.

databases.name: Google BigQuery (BigQuery ML + Vertex AI)
databases.ai_feature: BigQuery ML with Vertex AI and Gemini integration
databases.description: BigQuery ML lets analysts create, train, and run ML models using standard SQL (regression, classification, clustering, time series, boosted trees, matrix factorization) and call remote Vertex AI models including Gemini for text generation, embeddings, and multimodal tasks via ML.GENERATE_TEXT and ML.GENERATE_EMBEDDING.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. BigQuery provides a VECTOR_SEARCH function with vector indexes (IVF/TreeAH) for approximate nearest-neighbor search directly in SQL.
databases.llm_integration: Deep integration with Vertex AI Gemini and PaLM-family models plus embedding models through remote model objects invoked from SQL.
databases.pricing_notes: Billed via BigQuery on-demand bytes-processed or capacity slots; Vertex AI model calls incur separate Vertex AI usage charges per token/request.

databases.name: PostgreSQL (pgvector + pgai)
databases.ai_feature: pgvector for embeddings and pgai for in-database LLM workflows
databases.description: pgvector adds vector storage and similarity operators to Postgres, while pgai (from Timescale) and the pgai Vectorizer enable calling LLM/embedding providers (OpenAI, Cohere, Ollama, etc.) and automatically creating/maintaining embeddings via SQL, turning Postgres into a RAG-capable store.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native-via-extension. Core PostgreSQL has no built-in vector type, but pgvector is the de facto open-source extension providing vector columns and HNSW/IVFFlat indexes; it is first-party for the Postgres ecosystem though technically an extension.
databases.llm_integration: Through pgai, SQL functions proxy to external LLM and embedding APIs; LangChain and other frameworks commonly use pgvector as a backing vector store.
databases.pricing_notes: Open source and free; cost is limited to the hosting infrastructure plus any external LLM API usage. Managed providers may charge for compute/storage.

databases.name: Amazon Aurora ML
databases.ai_feature: Aurora Machine Learning — SQL integration with SageMaker and Bedrock
databases.description: Aurora ML lets you invoke ML models directly from SQL by calling Amazon SageMaker endpoints and Amazon Bedrock (including foundation models and embeddings) and Amazon Comprehend, so predictions and generative outputs are returned inline with query results without ETL.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native. Aurora itself does not provide a built-in vector search engine; vector capability on Aurora PostgreSQL-Compatible Edition comes only through the third-party pgvector extension, so native vector search is marked false.
databases.llm_integration: SQL-callable integration with Amazon Bedrock foundation models and SageMaker-hosted models for inference and embeddings.
databases.pricing_notes: No extra charge for the Aurora ML integration itself; you pay standard Aurora instance/storage costs plus the underlying SageMaker, Bedrock, or Comprehend usage.

databases.name: Amazon Redshift ML
databases.ai_feature: Redshift ML — in-warehouse model training and inference via SQL
databases.description: Redshift ML uses CREATE MODEL SQL statements to train models with Amazon SageMaker Autopilot (auto model selection and tuning), import existing models, or invoke remote SageMaker and Bedrock endpoints, enabling predictions and generative/LLM calls directly in analytical SQL queries.
databases.vector_search_notes: Not native in the core engine. Redshift does not ship a general-purpose built-in vector index; semantic retrieval is handled externally or via integrations, so native vector search is marked false (support for vector workloads has been evolving but is not a standard built-in search feature comparable to BigQuery/Snowflake).
databases.llm_integration: SQL functions can call Amazon Bedrock LLMs and SageMaker endpoints for generative and embedding tasks alongside built-in AutoML training.
databases.pricing_notes: Standard Redshift compute/storage charges plus SageMaker training and Bedrock inference costs; model training consumes SageMaker resources billed separately.

databases.name: Databricks (Mosaic AI + Vector Search)
databases.ai_feature: Mosaic AI platform with managed Vector Search
databases.description: Mosaic AI provides end-to-end GenAI tooling — model training and fine-tuning, model serving, Agent Framework, foundation model APIs, and governance via Unity Catalog — while Databricks Vector Search delivers a fully managed, serverless vector index synced to Delta tables for RAG and semantic search.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Databricks Vector Search is a first-party managed service that automatically indexes and syncs embeddings from Delta tables and serves ANN queries.
databases.llm_integration: Mosaic AI Model Serving hosts foundation models (Llama, DBRX, etc.) and external provider gateways; tight integration with LangChain and the Agent Framework for RAG pipelines.
databases.pricing_notes: Consumption-based using Databricks DBUs for compute, model serving, and vector search endpoints; pay-per-token foundation model APIs available.

databases.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
databases.ai_feature: Atlas Vector Search for semantic and hybrid retrieval
databases.description: Atlas Vector Search lets you store embeddings alongside operational JSON documents and run approximate nearest-neighbor queries using the $vectorSearch aggregation stage, supporting pre-filtering, hybrid search, and RAG directly within the operational database.
databases.vector_search_notes: Native. Vector Search is built into Atlas via dedicated vector indexes and the $vectorSearch aggregation operator, with HNSW-based ANN indexing managed by the platform.
databases.llm_integration: No built-in LLM hosting, but tight integrations with LangChain, LlamaIndex, OpenAI, and other embedding/LLM providers for building RAG applications on Atlas data.
databases.pricing_notes: Included with Atlas; vector search runs on cluster resources (or dedicated Search Nodes), so cost scales with cluster tier and Search Node provisioning rather than a separate license.
